Tucson, Arizona · eat

Restaurants in Tucson for cyclists

Where to eat in Tucson the night before a ride and the afternoon after. Nothing fancy. Real food, real portions, places that are open when you need them.

For: El Tour de Tucson.

Restaurants in Tucson for cyclists, listed

  1. Seis Kitchen (Mercado San Agustín)

    Mexican · 130 S Avenida del Convento #100, Tucson, AZ 85745

    After the ride, west side: in the Mercado San Agustín courtyard where the Women's Shootout (Saturdays, 7:15 am) meets, less than half a mile from the Loop. Breakfast from 8, until 11 on weekdays and noon on weekends, then lunch and dinner to 9. No reservations; you order, then they seat you, per its site. (520) 622-2002.

    Nearby ride: Women's Shootout Tucson (Saturdays, 7:15 am) →

  2. 5 Points Restaurant

    Brunch · 756 S Stone Ave, Tucson, AZ 85701

    After the ride, just south of downtown in Barrio Viejo and a short way from the convention center hotels: brunch 9 to 2 and dinner 5 to 9, Thursday to Monday, closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Book on Resy, patio tables too; dogs are welcome on the patio, and its site says it is easy to reach by bike. (520) 623-3888.

  3. Cup Cafe at Hotel Congress

    American cafe · 311 E Congress St, Tucson, AZ 85701

    After the ride, downtown: the café inside Hotel Congress, with a dining room and a patio that runs out into the hotel's plaza. No reservations for breakfast or lunch, per its page. The page gave no hours when we checked in October 2026; confirm before you go.

  4. El Charro Café (Downtown)

    Sonoran Mexican · 311 N Court Ave, Tucson, AZ 85701

    The night before, downtown. Open 11 to 9 every day, and it takes reservations, so a group can book ahead, per its site. (520) 622-1922.

  5. BOCA by Chef Maria Mazon

    Tacos · 533 N 4th Ave, Tucson, AZ 85705

    The night before, or late on a weekend, on Fourth Avenue: tacos on corn or flour tortillas with the house salsas, cooked to order. Noon to 9 Monday to Thursday, to 10 Friday and Saturday, to 8 Sunday, per its site. 520-777-8134.

  6. El Güero Canelo (Oracle)

    Sonoran hot dogs · 2480 N Oracle Rd, Tucson, AZ 85705

    Late, north of downtown on Oracle Road: Sonoran hot dogs, carne asada tacos and burros from a James Beard Award-winning restaurant, per its site. 11 to 10, and to 11 on Friday and Saturday. The two other locations, on East 22nd Street and South 12th Avenue, close at 10. (520) 882-8977.

  7. Tumerico

    Latin vegan · 2526 E 6th St, Tucson, AZ 85716

    The meat-free pick, midtown on Sixth Street: vegetarian and vegan Latin American plates. 11 to 8 Tuesday to Saturday, 10 to 4 Sunday, closed Monday, per its site, so it is an early dinner. 520-240-6947.

  8. Barrio Bread

    Bakery · 18 S Eastbourne Ave, Tucson, AZ 85716

    The one you'd go back for: Don Guerra's bakery; he won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Baker in 2022, per its site. Open 9 to 1 every day, or until it sells out, so go in the morning. 520-327-1292.
